title: Alexandr Wang on frontier data, model economics, and keeping headcount flat at Scale AI
summary: Wang explains why data is the next bottleneck for AI after compute and algorithms, and why renting out models is a weaker business than the layers above and below it. He also shares hiring lessons: keep high-performing teams small, onboard outside executives slowly, and stay in the key decisions as founder-CEO.

principles.text: Public data is exhausted, so the next AI advances depend on producing new, harder data.
principles.quote: we've kind of run out of all the easily accessible and easily available data out there

principles.text: Capabilities like agents are blocked by missing data, so you must produce data that doesn't exist yet.
principles.quote: it turns out there's just no agent data on the internet

principles.text: Pure model rental has weak pricing power; better businesses sit below (compute) and above (applications).
principles.quote: it turns out intelligence might be a commodity

principles.text: Scaling headcount erodes a high-performing team, so hold it flat while the business grows.
principles.quote: if you have a very high performing team and a very high performing org it's in near impossible to grow it dramatically without losing all that high performance

principles.text: Bring outside executives in slowly: small steps first, trust and verify, larger changes only after a track record.
principles.quote: they take small steps and you sort of like you trust and verify each of these small steps

principles.text: A founder-CEO should not outsource key decisions; making them well is the job.
principles.quote: the reason that you are a good founder CEO is because you make very good decisions over and over and over again
